title: Evolving volcanic surface-scattering evidence
notes: All plotted regional comparisons use the same pixels valid on every selected date or pair. Per-date coverage is shown separately; missing coverage is never reported as zero change.
Backscatter changes can reflect moisture, vegetation, roughness or geometry; they do not identify a cause by themselves.
Area uses the common valid analysis grid; local UTM areas are approximate. Coarse analysis cells are averages, not new high-resolution observations.
Latest changed patches can first appear on any later acquisition; absence on an earlier date no longer removes a late-growing patch.
Repeated latest change requires at least two consecutive post-baseline observations in the same direction. It is not proof of uninterrupted change between passes.
First-change indices identify sampled acquisition dates; onset lies in an unobserved interval, and may predate this record.
Smoothing uses a normalized Gaussian and preserves missing cells. Small signed patches are filtered in physical square metres.
Snowmelt, surface wetness, terrain effects and viewing geometry can change brightness. Candidate patches are not validated lava, temperature, volume or eruption probability.
A baseline acquired during an ongoing eruption measures later change only; existing lava with stable brightness may remain undetected.
Input is a local native-grid area extract, not a complete original NASA product; only the saved rectangle can be analyzed.
GCOV source-sample mask is applied before averaging. It is not a terrain-shadow or water classifier.

tracking.meaning: Dated candidate objects linked by overlap on a common analysis grid. Gaps are unobserved; links do not establish uninterrupted physical identity.

report.headline: What these observations show
findings: 5 compatible GCOV observations cover 2026-06-18 to 2026-08-17. Regional comparisons use 1,195,151 common analysis cells (478.060 km²).
Latest candidate change covers 145.603 km²; 128.292 km² is supported on at least two consecutive later observations in the same direction. These are scattering candidates, not validated lava.
The declared baseline is an observed starting state. Existing deposits may already be present; late-arriving patches and transient changes are kept separately.
report.comparison_basis: fixed common footprint across all selected observations
next_checks: Inspect observation counts and source quality before interpreting a pattern.
Compare the map and observed dates; blank pixels are missing evidence.
Use independent observations to test environmental attribution.
report.validation: Synthetic engineering tests check known calculations and missing-data behavior; independent real-world accuracy is not established.
